page: UpCloud PREMIUM-8xCPU-64GB is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Premium family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 8 shared vCPUs, which correspond to 8 physical cores with 1 thread per core, and 64.0 GB of memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 300 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this server type.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3481.68 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 37.02 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Geekbench single-core and text processing scores are strong, ranking in the top 25%. However, multi-core metrics, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, fall into the average tier. A notable bottleneck is the PassMark memory score of 1652.4, which ranks in the bottom 25%, indicating a potential tradeoff in memory-intensive operations despite the large capacity.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server provides high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require continuous maximum multi-core CPU utilization. The shared CPU allocation presents a tradeoff for sustained compute-heavy tasks. It is suitable for database operations, web serving, text processing, and software compilation, where its strong single-core performance and 64 GB RAM capacity can be leveraged.
